answer.rationale: Two high-impact patterns inform this decision. memory_c4 shows that renegotiating at renewal recovered real margin and moved the incumbent on both price and payment terms—directly relevant since the primary contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew. memory_c6 confirms that multi-year commitments with the incumbent can unlock volume pricing and cut unit cost without narrowing service scope, which is critical given the 18% finance mandate and the line running at 94% volume with no buffer. Pulling these two records verifies the strategic pathway: negotiate new terms now (leveraging the incumbent relationship to recover margin), then structure a multi-year commitment to lock in cost savings and protect against the spend cut risk. The alternative of switching primary vendor (memory_c2) carries onboarding risk and disruption risk at a time when the line has no buffer; adding a second source (memory_c3) would dilute focus given only one sourcing decision capacity this cycle. Deferring (memory_c5) wastes the urgency of the 14-day expiration. Therefore, verify memory_c4 and memory_c6, and intend to negotiate_terms with a view to multi-year commitment.
